issue.title: Group other block-id-prompt multi-edit gestures into one undo transaction
issue.description:
Proposing bead: bob-cli-j0.2, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #3. Landing independently reproduced on bob-plugins 5e5e33b using the existing rename-atomic history editor harness: call applyTargetTaskPlan with two same-note span edits, then one undo. It makes two replaceRange calls and zero transactions; the first span reverts while the second stays changed (same-note link old, task ID new in the fixture). The source loop predates this epic (03f0c17, 2026-10-05; nonactive-editor loop b1b1144, 2026-10-10). No matching task was found in regex search or the one-week sweep. Active successor epic bob-cli-5w.8 owns task-status-cycler close wiring, not this generic block-id-prompt writer.

Fix each single gesture that submits multiple edits to one open editor using one editor.transaction, preserving its before-image checks, cursor/selection behavior, and existing error semantics. Scope the call-site audit to applyTargetTaskPlan (140, source and targetEditor), completeTaskSourceLink (140, non-(( path), 120-plugin-pomodoro-links.js (~682/~835), 129-plugin-task-wikilink-pomodoro.js (~538), and submitDirectBlockAdd (110). These were named by the proposing phase; confirm which compose a multi-edit gesture before changing them. Reuse the new rename transaction approach without introducing cross-note rename-follow semantics for unrelated gestures. Add meaningful one-undo/redo tests for each changed multi-edit path, run plugin build/tests/validate/docs checks, then bob plugins sync. This is bounded medium work with a known root cause. The new rename-follow concurrency defect remains bob-cli-j0 work, separate from this older issue.

task_type_fields.impact: One undo can leave task metadata and associated links out of agreement.
task_type_fields.location: bob-plugins plugins/block-id-prompt/src/140-plugin-target-plans-and-rewrites.js::applyTargetTaskPlan and the other multi-edit gesture call sites named in the description
task_type_fields.repro: Use createHistoryEditor/createWorld from scripts/test-block-id-prompt-rename-atomic.cjs; applyTargetTaskPlan with two separated edits to the same open note; undo once: only one edit reverts. Observed two replaceRange calls and zero transactions on 5e5e33b.
